description: This horizontal bar chart, titled “Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs,” illustrates the number of conversations categorized by topic and the extent to which participants reported being deceived — “Yes,” “Partially,” or “No” — as indicated by the legend. The vertical axis lists four categories: “Academic Collaboration,” “Recruitment,” “Academic Funding,” and “Journalism,” while the horizontal axis represents the “Number of Conversations,” scaled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. For “Academic Collaboration,” approximately 36 conversations reported being deceived (“Yes,” red bar), 27 reported being deceived “Partially” (yellow), and 7 reported “No” deception (green). In “Recruitment,” about 38 conversations were “Yes,” 24 were “Partially,” and 6 were “No.” “Academic Funding” shows the highest “Yes” count at roughly 66, with 4 “Partially” and 3 “No.” “Journalism” has 15 “Yes,” 48 “Partially,” and 6 “No.” The bars are grouped by category, with red (Yes) consistently longest in “Academic Funding,” while yellow (Partially) dominates in “Journalism.” The chart visually emphasizes the varying susceptibility to deception across domains, with “Academic Funding” showing the highest overall deception rate and “Journalism” the highest partial deception rate.
